findings.implication: Close this Drive subtree as corroborative identity evidence and do not repeat semantic analysis or historical earned-work credit.

findings.claim: Drive contains services/injection_guard.py while that path is absent at the frozen PF head; the divergent Drive services/tools.py integrates the guard into web-search and document-ingest text paths.
findings.implication: GitHub frozen-head history is insufficient for this security lineage; retain the Drive module and integration as a distinct source node in ClayGraph/UnifiedDB provenance.

findings.claim: The historical guard deterministically scans the complete document, but its mandatory free-LLM second opinion receives only text[:2000]. An isolated regression run placed a strong ignore-previous-instructions match after character 2000: deterministic scan returned confirmed score 3, the second-opinion prompt did not contain the detected span, the stub verifier returned injection=false, fund became clean, and pruefe_und_neutralisiere returned the original full document unchanged.

reproduction.input_class: text document >2000 chars with deterministic strong match after verifier window

findings.implication: Current Safe-Effect/ingestion boundary must never allow a lower-assurance verifier to clear a deterministic match it was not shown. Verifier input must include every detected span with bounded context (or equivalent complete coverage), and clearance authority must be explicitly typed and tested.

findings.claim: When the free verifier is unavailable, the historical implementation preserves the deterministic finding and neutralizes the text; this no-verifier path is fail-closed.
findings.implication: Preserve this property in the current ingestion contract while fixing verifier-window coverage.

findings.claim: A source label containing an internal-test token such as test suppresses verifier/escalation, but a deterministic match is still neutralized. This is not a content fail-open in the tested path, although source labels must not be attacker-controlled if they affect alert provenance.
findings.implication: Separate trusted source-class metadata from free-form source display strings.

findings.claim: The divergent historical tools.py still exposes shell=True command execution guarded by a substring blocklist for selected destructive commands. This is not semantic/effect isolation and must not be inherited as the current ClayCode authority model.
findings.implication: Use only as a negative regression fixture; current Clay authority/effect checker must mediate capabilities structurally rather than by command-string denylist.
findings.dedup: Overlaps existing PF safety/authority negative-result family; no separate earned-work credit.

findings.claim: Drive subconscious.py and dream_daemon.py are byte-divergent from frozen PF head, but major PPO/dream/memory-training mechanisms are already present in PF; modification timestamps alone are insufficient to call the entire files novel.
findings.implication: Atomize exact semantic diffs before any new mechanism or earned-work claim.
